name: Cyrus Audio
_legal_entity: cyrusaudio.com has a goods-sale terms page and a separate copyright page reading « All materials on this website, unless otherwise stated, are Copyright 2017 of Cyrus Audio Ltd. » with the advice that « the copying of material protected by copyright law may require the permission of the copyright holders ». Both were READ: that is plain copyright language and advice, not a prohibition.
_merged_from_a_duplicate_file: cyrus-audio.json carried the same display name and a different id, and was deleted on 2026-11-25. The three Cyrus records all carry brand « cyrus », so that is the file that survives. I created cyrus.json earlier the SAME DAY while writing those records, without noticing cyrus-audio.json already sat beside it - the same mistake as Cambridge Audio, made first and seen second. Keys carried over: none, it held nothing new. Found by a new guard in the verifier that refuses two brand files claiming one name - added the same day after I created a fourth such duplicate by accident, which is how these three came to light. They had passed every check since they were written: the mutant suite tests that a RECORD cites a brand that exists, and most brand files here are census entries with no records, so « cited by nobody » could never have been the guard.
